evaluation_framework.description: Quantitative and qualitative assertions for validating the brand-governance-unifier skill

assertions.description: No contradictions between documents on core principles, communication style, or brand rules
assertions.scoring: Pass if all documents align on (a) complexity principle, (b) outcome-focused positioning, (c) executive vs. commercial voice separation, (d) no em-dashes rule

assertions.description: Philosophy consistently reinforced across all documents
assertions.scoring: Pass if 'we absorb complexity so customers experience clarity' is evident in every doc's structure and examples

assertions.description: Clear distinction between Executive (internal/leadership) and Commercial (customer-facing) voice
assertions.scoring: Pass if each document explicitly labels its intended audience and uses appropriate vocabulary/tone (elevated vs. Grade 8)

assertions.description: Concepts are not repeated across documents without cross-reference
assertions.scoring: Pass if no concept appears verbatim in multiple docs without explicit cross-reference. Measure: scan for duplicate paragraphs (allow <5% word-for-word overlap after consolidation)

assertions.description: Writing is clearer and more authoritative than originals
assertions.scoring: Pass if (a) sentences are shorter on average, (b) jargon is explained or removed, (c) tone is confident and restrained (not defensive or apologetic)

assertions.description: Each document has a clear, distinct purpose and role in the system
assertions.scoring: Pass if introduction to each document clearly states its role and how it relates to other docs. Measure: each doc must have <200-word role statement that distinguishes it from others

assertions.description: No references to old iterations, previous decisions, or historical paths
assertions.scoring: Pass if zero mentions of 'previously,' 'historically,' 'as we used to,' 'old approach,' or references to WebStaffr-clean. Measure: grep for legacy-reference keywords

assertions.description: WebStaffr-specific brand rules are documented and followed (Garamond, colors, no em dashes)
assertions.scoring: Pass if (a) brand rules section exists, (b) no em dashes found anywhere, (c) WebStaffr name styling documented, (d) color codes (#1f4d78 or split option) stated

assertions.description: Commercial voice documents are Grade 8 reading level or below
assertions.scoring: Measure via automated readability (Flesch-Kincaid Grade Level). Pass if commercial docs avg <8.0, executive docs avg 10.0-14.0

assertions.description: A clear reconciliation memo explains consolidation decisions
assertions.scoring: Pass if memo includes (a) which docs were consolidated/merged, (b) which kept separate and why, (c) contradictions found and how resolved, (d) new governance roles defined

assertions.description: 'Cutting-edge AI' vs. 'we fix your furnace' contradiction is resolved into coherent positioning
assertions.scoring: Pass if final copy positions company as (a) reliable outcome-focused partner, (b) reduces emphasis on AI/technology, (c) emphasizes customer benefit (comfort, peace of mind, speed)

assertions.description: Tone feels premium but tradesperson-friendly throughout
assertions.scoring: Pass if (a) no condescension toward customer, (b) simple language (Grade 8), (c) confidence without arrogance, (d) professionalism balanced with approachability

assertions.description: Each consolidated document has a distinct, non-overlapping role
assertions.scoring: Pass if visual doc covers design only, editorial covers voice/examples only, sales covers positioning only, with minimal cross-document repetition

assertions.description: Audit correctly identifies style guide violations in input docs
assertions.scoring: Pass if audit finds: (a) em-dashes, (b) tone inconsistency (casual on website vs. enterprise in sales), (c) vocabulary mismatch (high in investor pitch, casual elsewhere), (d) brand rule violations

assertions.description: Logo treatment and visual rules are clearly documented and enforced
assertions.scoring: Pass if visual governance includes (a) Garamond specifications, (b) size hierarchy, (c) color codes with hex values, (d) usage rules (when to use which variant)

assertions.description: Executive and Commercial voice are clearly separated and examples provided
assertions.scoring: Pass if guidance includes (a) example sentences in each style, (b) vocabulary lists (elevated vs. simple), (c) scenario guides (when to use which), (d) common pitfalls (don't do this)

assertions.description: Audit identifies all style guide violations in the sample copy
assertions.scoring: Pass if audit flags: (a) elevated vocabulary ('leverages paradigms'), (b) AI-focus contradiction, (c) 'not just' pattern violation, (d) em-dash use if present

assertions.description: Rewritten copy adheres to governance (Grade 8, outcome-focused, no em dashes)
assertions.scoring: Pass if rewrite is (a) simple and clear, (b) focuses on customer outcome not technology, (c) uses short sentences, (d) matches example tone from governance doc

assertions.description: Audit report clearly explains what was wrong and why
assertions.scoring: Pass if report includes (a) specific quote from original, (b) explanation of violation, (c) reference to governance rule, (d) suggested fix with reasoning
